description: Decision trail for AI agents. Each entry records a non-obvious decision, its rationale, and what an agent must NOT do. Source files reference these via '// @breadcrumb BC-NNN'. Validate with MachineCommentValidationTest.

entries.title: Process-wide engine, owner-scoped display
entries.decision: LvglEngine is a process-wide singleton; an activity binds/unbinds a display by owner identity instead of tearing the engine down.
entries.rationale: Tearing the engine down between activities showed the previous activity's screen and stalled the UI thread (ANR).
consequences: The native engine and its render thread outlive every activity.
A stale owner's deinitDisplay must be ignored.
do_not: Never call LvglEngine.shutdown() from an activity.
entries.ai_hint: When adding lifecycle code, reason about owner identity, not about activity destruction.

entries.title: Surface rebind fast path
entries.decision: On a same-size surface, keep the display and only rebind the ANativeWindow; do not tear the display down and rebuild it.
entries.rationale: Rebuilding the display on every activity transition both showed the wrong screen and wedged the UI thread (ANR).
consequences: A same-size initDisplay is a pure rebind.
A size change is the only case that rebuilds the display.
do_not: Do not join the render thread from the UI thread during a rebind.
entries.ai_hint: The fast path is the default; treat teardown as the exceptional branch.

entries.title: Never scheduleTask() under engine->mutex
entries.decision: Copy state under the lock, release it, and only then call scheduleTask().
entries.rationale: scheduleTask locks the same non-recursive mutex, so calling it while holding engine->mutex deadlocks the UI thread (ANR).
consequences: nativeSetScreen / nativeApplyTheme take the lock only to read flags.
A deadlock here presents as 'System UI isn't responding'.
do_not: Never call scheduleTask() while holding engine->mutex.
entries.ai_hint: Any new JNI entry point must follow the lock-copy-release-schedule pattern.

entries.title: Decorative LVGL objects must clear CLICKABLE/SCROLLABLE
entries.decision: Route every decorative object through decorative() so it cannot swallow taps from a clickable ancestor.
entries.rationale: A plain lv_obj is clickable by default; inner columns/labels captured presses so the card's LV_EVENT_CLICKED never fired.
consequences: Labels, accent bars and inner columns go through decorative().
Without it, taps silently do nothing.
do_not: Do not create a decorative container without clearing LV_OBJ_FLAG_CLICKABLE.
entries.ai_hint: If a tap handler never fires, suspect a decorative child stealing the hit test.

entries.title: Containers need explicit flex layout
entries.decision: Every container holding more than one child sets an explicit flex layout via make_row/make_column.
entries.rationale: A plain lv_obj has no layout, so all children are placed at (0,0) and overlap (card titles/subtitles stacked).
consequences: Multi-child containers must be created through the layout helpers.
Overlapping text is the symptom of a missing layout.
do_not: Do not add a second child to a container created with lv_obj_create().
entries.ai_hint: When two labels overlap, the parent has no layout set.

entries.title: LVGL fonts are fixed pixel sizes
entries.decision: Pick fonts through ui_font(dp, dpi) and spacing through dpx(dp, dpi); never use lv_font_montserrat_NN directly.
entries.rationale: LVGL fonts are fixed pixel sizes, so lv_font_montserrat_14 renders ~5sp text on a 440dpi display.
consequences: Montserrat ships only up to size 48; that is the ladder cap.
The enabled sizes must match lv_conf.h.
do_not: Do not reference lv_font_montserrat_56/64/72; they do not compile.
entries.ai_hint: Text that is unreadably small means a font was chosen in pixels instead of dp.

entries.title: BGRA to RGBA swap in the flush callback
entries.decision: Swap R/B channels per pixel in display_flush_cb before copying to the ANativeWindow.
entries.rationale: LVGL stores lv_color32_t as {blue,green,red,alpha}; Android RGBA_8888 expects {red,green,blue,alpha}.
consequences: Colors are inverted without the swap.
nativeCaptureFrame returns 0xRRGGBB ints, not raw memory.
do_not: Do not change the window format without re-checking the channel order.
entries.ai_hint: Red and blue swapping means the byte order assumption changed somewhere.

entries.title: Status text cached per screen id
entries.decision: Cache the last status text together with the screen id it belongs to, and re-apply it in rebuild_screen().
entries.rationale: onResume re-asserting the screen triggers a rebuild that reset the label to its initial text, so live status was wiped.
consequences: lastStatusScreen scopes the cache so text cannot leak between screens.
An onResume rebuild restores live status instead of losing it.
do_not: Do not apply cached status to a different screen id.
entries.ai_hint: If status resets after resume, the rebuild is not re-applying the cached text.

entries.title: Navigation bridge requires JNI_OnLoad
entries.decision: Store the JavaVM in JNI_OnLoad and cache method IDs in nativeSetNavCallback; drain requests on the LVGL thread.
entries.rationale: Removing JNI_OnLoad left g_vm null, so nav_valid() was always false and navigation silently failed.
consequences: Navigation only works if JNI_OnLoad is present.
Requests are drained by the LVGL thread, never the UI thread.
do_not: Do not call Kotlin from native on a thread that is not attached to the JVM.
entries.ai_hint: Silent navigation failure means g_vm or the cached method IDs are missing.

entries.title: LvglActivity subclasses must not setContentView()
entries.decision: Activities extending LvglActivity must not call setContentView(); switch content via LvglEngine.setScreen().
entries.rationale: setContentView replaces the LVGL SurfaceView and produces the greyed-out 'System UI isn't responding' screen.
consequences: The base class owns the root layout and SurfaceView.
Use AppCompatActivity when native Android views are needed.
do_not: Do not call setContentView() from a LvglActivity subclass.
entries.ai_hint: A greyed-out UI after a screen switch is almost always a setContentView regression.

entries.title: Re-assert screen id on resume
entries.decision: LvglActivity records its screen id and re-asserts it in onResume when the display shows a different screen, skipping the first resume.
entries.rationale: The display is process-wide, so returning to an activity that never re-requested its screen showed the wrong screen.
consequences: firstResume skips the redundant initial request.
Only a differing screen id triggers a rebuild, avoiding flicker.
do_not: Do not rebuild the screen on every resume unconditionally.
entries.ai_hint: Wrong screen after back navigation means onResume is not re-asserting the id.

entries.title: DIRECT render mode, full-screen framebuffer
entries.decision: Use LV_DISPLAY_RENDER_MODE_DIRECT with two full-screen framebuffers.
entries.rationale: Partial rendering had ANativeWindow swapchain issues.
consequences: The flush callback always copies the full display.
Two buffers avoid tearing between LVGL and the window.
do_not: Do not switch to partial rendering without fixing the swapchain path.
entries.ai_hint: A black screen usually means buffers were set after the flush callback.

entries.title: LV_THEME_DEFAULT_LIGHT is undefined in LVGL 9.6.0
entries.decision: Define LV_THEME_DEFAULT_LIGHT as 0 when the header does not provide it.
entries.rationale: LVGL 9.6.0 does not define the light theme constant, so referencing it fails to compile.
consequences: Light mode uses 0; dark mode uses LV_THEME_DEFAULT_DARK.
The fallback must stay guarded by #ifndef.
do_not: Do not reference LV_THEME_DEFAULT_LIGHT without the #ifndef guard.
entries.ai_hint: A missing light-theme symbol means the guard was removed or LVGL changed.

entries.title: Guard tests must fail loudly and prove they detect violations
entries.decision: Guard tests locate the repo root by walking up, assert the path exists, and include canary fixtures that must be detected (and clean fixtures that must not be).
entries.rationale: A hardcoded relative path once resolved outside the repo, so exists() was false and two of three rules silently no-opped (false green).
consequences: A broken path fails the suite instead of passing it.
Each detector is proven to catch a real violation and to ignore a clean fixture.
do_not: Do not weaken a detector until its canary test is updated too.
entries.ai_hint: If a guard goes green after a regression, its canary is missing or broken.

entries.title: Machine-readable comment schema and breadcrumb trail
entries.decision: Source files carry structured @tag annotations that cross-reference this trail; MachineCommentValidationTest parses and validates every annotation in the repo.
entries.rationale: AI agents need a machine-readable trail of non-obvious decisions instead of prose scattered across markdown.
consequences: Every annotation must use a known tag and a resolvable reference.
Orphaned breadcrumbs and dangling references fail the build.
do_not: Do not add an annotation with an unknown tag or a dangling BC-/ADR- reference.
entries.ai_hint: New non-obvious decisions should get a BC entry plus an in-code @breadcrumb.

entries.title: Demo UI is a single source of truth
entries.decision: All demo/sample screens are declared in demo_ui.h and implemented in demo_ui.cpp; the port only owns the engine and JNI.
entries.rationale: Splitting UI code across the port and demo files duplicated screens and made the widget set drift.
consequences: Screens are added by declaring a builder in demo_ui.h.
The port calls launch_screen() and nothing else UI-specific.
do_not: Do not build screens directly in lvgl_port.cpp.
entries.ai_hint: A screen change belongs in demo_ui.cpp, not the engine.

entries.title: Public ui_* UI-kit API
entries.decision: demo_ui.h declares the public UI-kit API (ui_make_panel, ui_make_column, ui_make_label, ui_decorative, ui_dpx, ui_dpi) and demo_ui.cpp defines it; demo_showcase.cpp consumes it.
entries.rationale: The showcase demo is a separate translation unit, so the helpers it uses must have external linkage and match the header exactly.
consequences: The ui_* helpers are non-static in demo_ui.cpp.
Renaming a helper requires updating demo_ui.h, demo_ui.cpp and every consumer.
A mismatch surfaces as an ld.lld undefined-symbol error, not a compile error.
do_not: Do not declare a ui_* helper in demo_ui.h without defining it in demo_ui.cpp.
entries.ai_hint: If the link fails on a ui_* symbol, the header and demo_ui.cpp have drifted.

entries.title: Frame callback lifetime
entries.decision: Engine::reset() must not clear the frame callback; the showcase sets it while the screen is built and clears it via ui_reset_showcase() when the screen is left.
entries.rationale: The render thread starts after the screen is built and calls Engine::reset(); clearing the callback there left the showcase without its per-frame driver, so windows never animated.
consequences: Engine::reset() clears springs/points/colors but keeps frame_callback_.
ui_reset_showcase() clears the callback and resets g_show before lv_obj_clean().
launch_screen() calls ui_reset_showcase() whenever the target is not the showcase.
do_not: Do not clear frame_callback_ in Engine::reset().
entries.ai_hint: If a window never animates, check whether the frame callback survived Engine::reset().

entries.title: Window overlay must ignore the parent layout
entries.decision: The window's backdrop and container carry LV_OBJ_FLAG_FLOATING so they ignore the parent's flex layout.
entries.rationale: A 2000x2000 backdrop in a flex column consumed the column and pushed the tiles off-screen; LVGL also ignores lv_obj_set_pos() for children of a laid-out parent.
consequences: Both bg_close_ and container_ are FLOATING.
The container's animated x/y via lv_obj_set_pos() is honoured.
do_not: Do not add a large overlay as a plain child of a flex parent.
entries.ai_hint: If an overlay makes siblings vanish, it is participating in the parent's layout.

entries.title: Dashboard replaces the list menu as the home screen
entries.decision: Screen id 0 (SCREEN_HOME) builds the M5Tab5-style device dashboard: a full-screen Android system schematic with floating control panels and a status bar; the seven samples are reached from a Demos panel.
entries.rationale: The old list menu was generic. The reference device's look is a dashboard of floating panels over a schematic, and keeping every sample reachable satisfies the no-feature-removals hard rule.
consequences: SCREEN_HOME is the entry screen; the list menu screen no longer exists.
All seven samples remain reachable from the Demos panel on the dashboard.
do_not: Do not remove a sample from the Demos panel.
entries.ai_hint: Adding a sample means adding a row to kDemos plus a screen builder, not a new home screen.

entries.title: Schematic is drawn with LVGL primitives, not an image asset
entries.decision: The dashboard schematic is rendered from lv_obj rectangles, lv_line buses and labels in a 100x100 design space scaled to the diagram's pixel rectangle.
entries.rationale: A bitmap background would need an asset pipeline and would not scale across phone densities and orientations; primitives stay core-only and DPI-adaptive.
consequences: Chip layout is the kChips table of names, sub-labels, relative positions and bus colours.
One layout renders in portrait and landscape via non-uniform scaling.
do_not: Do not replace the schematic with a fixed-pixel bitmap.
entries.ai_hint: If chips overlap in portrait, adjust the kChips percentages rather than the drawing code.

entries.title: Status bar clock is an lv_timer torn down with its screen
entries.decision: The status bar and RTC panel share one 1 s lv_timer; make_screen deletes it before lv_obj_clean so it never touches freed labels. The battery level is pushed from Kotlin and cached.
entries.rationale: lv_timer objects survive lv_obj_clean, so a timer left running would dereference labels freed by the next screen build.
consequences: g_clock_timer is deleted at the top of make_screen().
The native side caches the battery level and re-applies it on dashboard build.
do_not: Do not create the clock timer without deleting it on screen change.
entries.ai_hint: A frozen clock after switching screens means the timer was deleted; a crash means it was not.

entries.title: Backlight and volume panels drive real Android APIs
entries.decision: The dashboard's backlight/volume panels call ui_set_system_hooks; the port forwards them through the ScreenNavigator's optional setBrightness/setVolumePercent methods to LvglSystemControl, which applies window brightness and the music stream volume.
entries.rationale: The reference device's control panels are functional; on Android the equivalent effects are per-window brightness and AudioManager volume. PowerManager.goToSleep() needs the system-only DEVICE_POWER permission, so the Power panel stays simulated.
consequences: LvglEngine.ScreenNavigator has default no-op system methods and the native bridge resolves them optionally.
LvglSystemControl is the single source of truth for these Android calls.
Window brightness must be posted to the UI thread; AudioManager is thread-safe and is called directly.
do_not: Do not call PowerManager.goToSleep() from an app, set screenBrightness below 1%, or touch WindowManager assets from the LVGL thread.
entries.ai_hint: If a panel tap does nothing, check that the navigator implements setBrightness/setVolumePercent, that the method IDs resolved, and that view changes are posted to the UI thread.

entries.title: Short taps are held until LVGL polls them once
entries.decision: The native touch path holds a press until LVGL has observed it: touch_read_cb reports PRESSED while touchPressSeen is false, and nativeTouchEvent clears that flag on ACTION_DOWN.
entries.rationale: LVGL polls the input device once per rendered frame, and with software GL a frame can take hundreds of milliseconds. A tap whose DOWN/UP pair lands entirely between two polls was never seen as pressed and produced no click.
consequences: A tap registers no matter how short, even when frames are very slow.
The press is held for at most one LVGL poll after a real press, so long-press timing is unaffected.
do_not: Do not clear touchPressSeen before LVGL has polled the press.
entries.ai_hint: If a tap is dropped only on a slow frame, check that the press-held flag is cleared on ACTION_DOWN and set once LVGL polls it.

entries.title: Navigator is restored in onResume
entries.decision: LvglActivity stores its ScreenNavigator in a field, re-registers it in onResume when the engine's navigator is no longer the same object, and only clears it in onDestroy while it is still this activity's.
entries.rationale: A child activity that is destroyed sets the engine's navigator to null; relying on onCreate alone left the parent's dashboard unable to navigate (nav_valid() false) after BACK. The parent's onResume also runs BEFORE the child's onDestroy, so an unconditional clear would wipe the freshly restored bridge.
consequences: Returning from a sample with BACK restores LVGL navigation.
The navigator is a field rather than an anonymous object created in onCreate.
onDestroy compares identity before clearing, so it never clobbers a sibling's bridge.
do_not: Do not rely on onCreate alone to keep the navigator registered.
entries.ai_hint: If dashboard taps do nothing after returning from a screen, check nav_valid() and whether the navigator was re-registered.

entries.title: Design tokens, scaffold, primitives and layout lint
entries.decision: The UI kit is built on a token scale (spacing/radius/type), every screen uses ui_make_scaffold (status bar + header + scrollable body), layout primitives always set a flex layout/gap/alignment, text auto-fits its box, and a native layout lint reports overlaps, out-of-bounds children and clipped text to logcat and a JSON report.
entries.rationale: Screenshots showed overlapping status-bar items, clipped chip text, a scrollbar covering a stepper button and unbalanced sample screens. Tokens and a scaffold remove whole classes of alignment mistakes, and the lint makes regressions visible in CI instead of in screenshots.
consequences: UiTokens is the single source of truth for spacing, radius and type sizes.
ui_make_scaffold is used by every sample screen.
Layout primitives (ui_make_row/column/grid/card/section/list_row) set a layout by construction.
ui_fit_label shrinks text to fit instead of clipping.
The lint runs after the first refresh of every screen and logs LVGLLayout warnings.
LvglEngine.dumpLayoutReport() exposes the same issues as JSON for the harness.
An empty LV_SIZE_CONTENT container in a flex row resolves to a 480 px default height in this LVGL build; spacers need an explicit height.
do_not: Do not hard-code spacing/radius/font sizes in new screens; use ui_tokens() and the primitives.
Do not leave an empty LV_SIZE_CONTENT child in a flex row without an explicit height.
entries.ai_hint: If a screen looks misaligned, run the lint (LVGLLayout logcat tag) before eyeballing screenshots.

entries.title: Dashboard device map reflects the real device
entries.decision: LvglDeviceInfo collects real device facts (Build, ActivityManager.MemoryInfo, StatFs, DisplayMetrics, CameraManager, SensorManager) and pushes them through nativeSetDeviceInfo; ui_set_device_info stores them and ui_make_diagram renders them inside a phone outline with a system bus.
entries.rationale: The previous schematic was hard-coded with generic labels, so it said the same thing on every device. Real values make the map a genuine system overview and a useful demonstration of the Android APIs.
consequences: LvglDeviceInfo.socMarketingName maps platform ids to marketing names with a readable fallback.
LvglActivity collects and pushes the facts in onCreate, before the dashboard is built.
nativeSetDeviceInfo copies the JNI strings into engine-owned storage; rebuild_screen copies them onto the LVGL thread before building.
Values the Android APIs do not expose (modem generation, WiFi standard, battery chemistry) show a plausible default.
Map chips position their two lines explicitly instead of using flex, so the lines always fit and never spread to the chip edges.
do_not: Do not hard-code device values in the UI.
entries.ai_hint: If the map shows wrong values, check that pushDeviceInfo runs before the first dashboard build.

entries.title: Material 3 tonal palette with dynamic color
entries.decision: MaterialPalette defines the 20 Material 3 tonal roles in a fixed index order, MaterialTheme resolves them from the baseline scheme or the Android system accents (API 31+), and nativeApplyTheme pushes the whole IntArray to LVGL; make_palette derives every UI colour from those roles.
entries.rationale: The previous theme passed only primary/secondary, so surfaces, text and chips were hard-coded and did not follow dark mode or Material You. A full tonal palette lets every component re-theme by construction.
consequences: MaterialPalette role indexes are shared with the native MaterialRole enum; reordering breaks the palette.
MaterialTheme follows the system dark/light mode and can pin an app-local override (the dashboard theme FAB).
Dynamic color reads system_accent1/2/3_500 on API 31+ and falls back to the baseline scheme below.
nativeApplyTheme rebuilds the current screen when the palette changes.
do_not: Do not reorder the MaterialPalette role constants; native indexes into the array.
Do not hard-code colours in the UI kit; read ui_palette().
entries.ai_hint: If colours look wrong after a theme change, verify the palette index order matches MaterialRole.

entries.title: Material 3 component kit on top of LVGL
entries.decision: A native component kit (buttons, chips, FAB, cards, text field, bottom nav, dialog, snackbar, top app bar) renders Material 3 from the tonal palette, and the sample app uses it for the dashboard controls and the widget showcase gallery.
entries.rationale: Apps should look and behave natively while staying pure LVGL. Hand-rolled widgets drifted from Material; a shared kit makes every app native-looking by construction.
consequences: Every component reads ui_palette()/ui_tokens(), so it re-themes with the active palette.
Buttons come in filled/tonal/outlined/text styles plus a danger variant.
Dialogs and snackbars are FLOATING overlays; the layout lint ignores them.
The dashboard theme FAB toggles an app-local dark-mode override through the ScreenNavigator bridge.
The widget showcase demonstrates the whole kit in its MATERIAL 3 section.
do_not: Do not hand-roll Material widgets; use the kit so they re-theme.
Do not position a FAB/dialog/snackbar without LV_OBJ_FLAG_FLOATING.
entries.ai_hint: If a new control does not follow the theme, make it read ui_palette() instead of hard-coded colours.

entries.title: Balanced APK size optimisation
entries.decision: Release builds enable R8 full mode, tree-shaking and resource shrinking, per-ABI splits, the static C++ STL, legacy native packaging and English-only resources; the size budget is 4 MB per ABI and 6 MB universal.
entries.rationale: The unminified universal release was 8.4 MB. The balanced target was ~4 MB per ABI while keeping the universal APK available.
consequences: Per-ABI release APKs are ~1.3 MB; the universal APK is ~2.1 MB.
libc++_shared.so is gone: the STL is linked into liblvgl_android.so.
The library module keeps isMinifyEnabled=false because enabling it makes lintVitalRelease report false-positive Instantiatable errors.
tools/size-report.ps1 enforces the budget in CI.
do_not: Do not enable isMinifyEnabled on the library module.
Do not remove the universal APK.
entries.ai_hint: If the size budget regresses, run tools/size-report.ps1 and check the largest APK entries.

entries.title: Developer toolkit: docs, template, plugin, API dump
entries.decision: The repo ships a quickstart, a public API reference, a copyable template/ Gradle project, a build-logic plugin that scaffolds a new LVGL app module, consumer ProGuard rules and a binary-compatibility API dump.
entries.rationale: Building an app on the framework should take minutes, not a copy of the sample app. The API dump makes releases predictable.
consequences: template/ builds against the local library via a composite build and the com.lvgl.android:lvgl-android coordinate.
build-logic provides the com.lvgl.android.app plugin and the createLvglApp task.
api/lvgl-android.api is checked in CI by :lvgl-android:apiCheck.
lvgl-android/consumer-rules.pro keeps the JNI entry points and public API.
do_not: Do not modify the sample app to scaffold a new app; use the template or the plugin.
entries.ai_hint: For a new app, copy template/ or run createLvglApp; do not duplicate the sample.

entries.title: Kotlin UI builder for app-defined LVGL screens
entries.decision: Apps declare their own LVGL screens in Kotlin with the LvglUiScope DSL; the tree is serialised to JSON, pushed through LvglEngine.registerScreen and rendered by lvgl_ui.cpp with the shared Material 3 UI kit. Interactions come back as typed LvglUiEvents, and updateNode() patches a node on the LVGL thread.
entries.rationale: The public API was screen-level only: an app could pick one of eight built-in screens but could not build its own UI. A declarative Kotlin DSL makes the framework genuinely usable while reusing the native kit, so there is still one source of truth for widget styling.
consequences: App screen ids start at APP_SCREEN_BASE (1000); 0..7 are the built-in screens.
The DSL supports column/row/label/button/slider/switch/checkbox/progress/arc/divider/spacer.
Node ids are auto-assigned (n0, n1, ...) unless the DSL id parameter is used.
updateNode() marshals to the LVGL thread; the node builder also runs there via launch_screen().
The native side carries a hand-rolled JSON reader to avoid a JSON dependency.
do_not: Do not build app screens from the UI thread; ui_build_app_screen runs on the LVGL thread.
Do not use app screen ids below 1000.
entries.ai_hint: For a new screen, register it with LvglUi.registerScreen and show it with setLvglScreen(id).

entries.title: Standard KDoc tags allowed in the comment schema
entries.decision: MachineCommentParser recognises the standard KDoc documentation tags (param, return, property, throws, exception, see, since, deprecated, author, sample, suppress) in addition to the machine tags. They are documentation-only and are never validated as machine annotations.
entries.rationale: The KDoc pass added @param/@return tags, which the machine-comment validator rejected as unknown tags. KDoc tags are prose, not key=value annotations, so they belong to documentation rather than the machine schema.
consequences: MachineCommentParser.KNOWN_TAGS = machine tags + KDOC_TAGS.
AnnotationValidator has no branch for KDoc tags, so they are accepted and ignored.
docs/agent-comment-schema.md documents the distinction.
do_not: Do not use a KDoc tag to carry machine-readable data; add a machine tag instead.
entries.ai_hint: If a new documentation tag is needed, add it to KDOC_TAGS rather than the machine tag list.

entries.title: Google Play compatibility
entries.decision: The app targets API 36, ships 64-bit ABIs and an AAB, declares backup/data-extraction rules, opts into predictive back, exposes a locale config, requests only the optional CAMERA permission, and discloses its open-source licences in-app.
entries.rationale: Google Play requires a recent target API, 64-bit support, an AAB, runtime permissions, a privacy policy, data-safety disclosure and open-source licence notices.
consequences: PlayComplianceGuardTest machine-checks the target API, ABIs, manifest attributes, permissions, privacy policy and licence screen.
PRIVACY.md and docs/play-store.md document the privacy policy and the release checklist.
The CAMERA permission remains optional; the app is fully usable without it.
do_not: Do not add a permission without a Play policy justification.
Do not remove the licence disclosure or the privacy policy.
entries.ai_hint: Run PlayComplianceGuardTest before a release; it fails the build on a Play regression.
